subject: Urgent: Significant latency and incorrect outputs after model upgrade / immediate rollback requested
messages:
From: Sofia Gomez <sofia.gomez@finservcorp.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@finservcorp.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production spike — latency + incorrect outputs after model push (impacting loan-approval pipeline)

Hannah,

We started seeing a large increase in p95/p99 latency and a spike in malformed completions after the new model version rolled at ~08:45 PT this morning. Our automated checks flagged:

- p95 latency up from 120ms to 620ms (for short prompts)
- p99 latency to ~1.8s in peak windows
- Error rate (invalid JSON in structured responses) rose from 0.2% -> 3.7%
- Throughput dropped ~18% under our steady load tests

Attached are the perf logs and a short list of customer examples (customer_examples.txt). This is impacting the loan-approval automation (DFC-3892) — under SLA we are required to have 99.9% availability and sub-300ms median latency for this route.

We need an immediate rollback to the previous model/version and confirmation of the mitigation plan. We can make an exec bridge available now.

Sofia
Sofia Gomez
Sr. Platform Reliability Engineer
FinServ Corp

Attachments: perf_logs_20260315.zip, customer_examples.txt

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Production spike — latency + incorrect outputs after model push (impacting loan-approval pipeline)

On Sun, 15 Mar 2026 at 09:12, Sofia Gomez <sofia.gomez@finservcorp.com> wrote:
> We started seeing a large increase in p95/p99 latency and a spike in malformed completions after the new model version rolled at ~08:45 PT this morning.

Quick summary from infra side:
- Deployment: redwood-model-alpha-v2.1-q5_1 pushed at 08:45 PT (release tag: v2.1-20260315, commit 7f3b9a4)
- Change: default quantization profile moved from q4_0 -> q5_1 to improve memory footprint for RB-GPU nodes; also a kernel switch optimized for long-sequence batching applied.
- Observed: KV-cache eviction frequency increased under typical short-prompt patterns, which increased token-generation latency. Additionally, for structured-output routes we are seeing occasional tokenization mismatch causing malformed JSON for a small fraction of seeds.

Immediate options:
1) Roll back to v2.0 in the affected pool (fastest, ~6-8min with current playbook).
2) Re-deploy v2.1 with q4_0 quant profile only (medium risk, needs validation).
3) Live patch: force short-prompt routing to a legacy kernel for 30m (mitigates p99 but requires routing changes).

I recommend option 1 while we investigate root cause; preparing rollback playbook now (attached). Will monitor logs and report within 10 minutes.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: rollback_playbook.md, perf_snippet_09_34.txt

- We will offer a one-time service credit for the incident and provide a short post-mortem within 48 hours.
- Can you confirm if the loan-approval pipeline has any manual failover in the meantime (we can route to an emergency fallback model)?

Also proposing a 4pm PT exec sync if you prefer to have senior leadership on the call — we can arrange.

- Request: approve immediate targeted rollback to v2.0 for FinServ pool and authorize up to 5% one-time credit on March invoice if confirmed degraded (Marcus to finalize amount).

Subject: Re: Production spike — latency + incorrect outputs after model push (impacting loan-approval pipeline)

Sofia — rollback to redwood-model-alpha-v2.0 completed on the affected pool at 09:58 PT. Immediate telemetry:
- p95 latency back to ~130ms, p99 ~280ms
- Structured-output error rate back down to 0.25%
- Throughput restored to expected range

What we did:
- Executed targeted rollback per rollback_playbook.md
- Disabled q5_1 quant profile for the FinServ pool and pinned v2.0
- Keeping enhanced sampling and verbose logs for 2 hours to validate stability

Next steps:
- Post-mortem scheduled: 2026-03-16 11:00 PT (INF-4721)
- Engineering will reproduce the tokenization mismatch locally and create a mitigation branch; we’ll triage quantization kernels for short-sequence patterns.

Apologies for the disruption. Please confirm that FinServ sees recovered metrics on your side; we will keep the bridge open for one hour.

— Dev
